transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I came in because, well, I just keep beating myself up lately. I've got this job as a systems analyst, and I just can't shake the feeling that I’m not really senior material. Like I’ve just somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

Which is funny because I've been messing with computers since high school. Never even needed a college degree for it, you know? I built my first rig when I was, like, fifteen. It was this old Pentium setup with a massive CRT monitor that weighed half a ton. My mom made me keep it down in the basement because she said it ruined the feng shui of the house. She got really into feng shui for a few years back then. Bought all these little indoor water fountains and made us keep the bathroom doors closed at all times so the positive energy wouldn't flush down the toilet. I'm pretty sure she just liked making my dad move the heavy furniture around every weekend, to be honest. He actually blew his back out moving a mahogany credenza in '98... 

But, um, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I just feel like I've tricked them all into giving me responsibilities I can't manage.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge about being found out as not competent at your job?

Anxious? No, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or on edge about it. I don't sit around sweating that someone's gonna march in and fire me or anything. It's not a panicky feeling. 

I don't really get anxious, to be honest, unless I drink way too much caffeine. Actually, I had this nitro cold brew last week that made my heart feel like it was gonna beat right out of my chest. My buddy Dave roasts his own beans in his garage. He bought this massive commercial roaster off eBay, and he had to rewire his whole electrical panel just to plug the thing in. I helped him with some of the low-voltage stuff for the temperature sensors since I know my way around a circuit board, but I told him he was crazy messing with the main breaker himself. Electricity is no joke. My uncle actually got a nasty shock once trying to fix a toaster while it was still plugged in. Blew the transformer for the whole street. The power company was so mad... 

But, um... wait, sorry. Anxious. Right. No, I don't really get on edge about work. It's just more of a heavy, sinking feeling that I don't measure up, you know? Not really an on-edge kind of thing.
Do you often feel sad or depressed?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. Most days lately I’ve just had this heavy, low feeling... like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down, you know? 

Actually, speaking of the color being turned down, it kind of reminds me of this old TV my grandparents used to have. It was one of those massive wooden console ones from the seventies. The color tube started going out on it, so everything had this weird, faded gray tone. We watched the '86 World Series on that thing, and you couldn't even tell the Mets' uniforms had blue in them. My grandfather refused to buy a new one because he said they didn't make them like they used to. He was a mechanic—worked on diesel engines his whole life—so he thought he could fix anything. He spent three weekends trying to solder a new capacitor onto the board of that TV, and ended up just melting half the plastic casing. My grandmother was so mad. She wouldn't let him watch his bowling tournaments in the living room for a month... 

But, uh... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling sad. Yeah, just... just that heavy, faded feeling. Like I said.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

Not really, no. I mean, usually I really look forward to grilling on the weekend, or maybe going fishing, or just putting on a record. But lately, I just leave all that stuff sitting there and I don't really care. 

Which is a shame, because I have this really nice offset smoker. I got it a few years back. My neighbor, Gary, he saw it and immediately had to go out and buy a way more expensive pellet grill. Gary's just one of those guys who has to one-up everyone, you know? Like last winter, I bought a snowblower, and two days later he’s got this massive two-stage beast that could clear an airport runway. Anyway, he tried smoking a brisket on that pellet thing for the Fourth of July block party last year, and he totally dried it out. Tasted like shoe leather. He blamed the butcher, but I saw him opening the lid every ten minutes to check it. You can't do that, you lose all the heat and the smoke. "If you're lookin', you ain't cookin'," that's what they say. My dad taught me that. He used to barbecue every single Sunday, rain or shine... 

But, um, wait. Sorry. Hobbies, right. Yeah, my grill is just sitting out there under the tarp right now. I just haven't had the interest to even uncover it or listen to any of my albums. Just don't care to.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, low feeling?

Looking back, I guess it’s been a while. Maybe around eleven months? I remember because it started right around the time we were doing this massive server migration at work. We were finally moving our databases off these ancient hardware blades to a cloud setup. My manager, Todd, insisted we do the entire cutover over a long weekend to minimize downtime. Which, you know, sounds great in theory, but it was a total disaster because the software vendor’s support team was on a skeleton crew. I told Todd we needed at least three of our own guys on standby, but he wanted to save the department budget on overtime. Typical Todd. He drives this leased BMW and always manages to slip his golf handicap into every conversation, but he doesn't know the first thing about actual network latency. 

Anyway, the migration script failed halfway through, and I spent 48 hours straight in the server room trying to roll back the system, just living on stale donuts and Diet Mountain Dew. I think I slept under my desk for two hours on a pile of ethernet cables. My neck was messed up for a week after that. I actually had to go to a chiropractor, which I usually think is a scam, but this guy had this weird table that sort of dropped out from under you...

But, uh... wait, sorry. I'm getting off track again. You asked how long. Right. Yeah, looking back to that migration, it was around then. So for about eleven months, off and on, these low, guilty periods have just been hanging around.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy most of the time?

Yeah, I think we... didn't we just talk about this? But yeah, like I said, most of the time now I just don't care. I mean, usually I'd be all about firing up the smoker on a Saturday, or maybe heading out to the lake with my tackle box, or just throwing on some classic rock vinyl. But now? The grill's under a tarp, my rods are gathering dust in the garage, and I haven't touched my turntable in weeks. 

Speaking of the garage, I really need to get in there and reorganize. I have this whole pegboard system I started putting up, but I ran out of the right size hooks. I went to the hardware store—that big box one out on Route 9—and they were completely out of the two-inch straight hooks. The guy working in that aisle, he couldn't have been more than eighteen, he tried to tell me the curved ones would work just as well for hanging extension cords. I was like, kid, you clearly don't understand weight distribution. If you hang a heavy-duty outdoor cord on a curved hook, it creates a pinch point and damages the insulation over time. My old shop teacher, Mr. Henderson, drilled that into our heads back in high school. He was missing half his left index finger from a bandsaw accident, so when he gave you safety or tool advice, you listened. He used to drive this beat-up El Camino that he restored himself...

But, um... sorry. What was the question? Right, losing interest. Yeah, most of the time, I just don't have the drive to do the things I normally like. Just kind of leave it all sitting there.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Well, I'm not really trying to, but yeah, my belt is definitely a little looser lately. My appetite has just been off. Mostly I'm just grabbing a few bites here and there, or skipping supper entirely. 

Which is weird for me, because I usually love to cook. Like I was saying about the smoker. I actually have this great recipe for a dry rub that I use on pork shoulders. It's got smoked paprika, brown sugar, a little cayenne, and this secret ingredient—ground espresso beans. I got the idea from this barbecue joint my wife and I went to on our honeymoon down in Austin. Place was literally just a shack by the side of the highway, no air conditioning, just picnic tables out back. But the line was out the door by 10 AM. We waited for two hours in the blazing Texas heat. My wife got so sunburned on her shoulders, she had to wear my oversized t-shirt for the rest of the trip. We actually went to a pharmacy to get aloe, and the pharmacist there was this older lady who insisted we also buy this weird herbal tea she swore would help with the inflammation. Tasted like dirt and licorice, honestly. I don't know why we actually drank it...

But, uh... wait. Weight, right. Yeah, I'm not trying to diet or anything, but I've definitely lost some weight because I just haven't been eating much supper or having much of an appetite.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you joy?

Yeah, I mean, I feel like we just covered this, but yeah. It's the same thing. I just... I don't get any joy out of it anymore. Like I said, normally I'd be all over grilling on the weekend, or heading out to fish, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don't really care. 

It's weird because I actually bought this new lure a couple months ago, right before I started feeling like this. It's this topwater frog lure, supposed to be incredible for bass when they're hiding out in the lily pads. I got it from this little bait shop near the lake. The guy who runs it, Sal, he's a character. Always wears these suspenders with measuring tapes printed on them. He was telling me about how the lake levels have been dropping the last few years because of some new dam project upstream. He said the Army Corps of Engineers completely botched the environmental impact study. According to Sal, they didn't even account for the migratory patterns of the local waterfowl, which is crazy because if you've ever been out there in October, the geese are everywhere. I mean, they make a huge mess on the docks. Last year I spent two hours power washing the community dock just so my wife wouldn't complain about slipping on... 

But, um... yeah. Pleasure. I just... I don't feel anything when I look at my grill or my fishing gear. It's just stuff now.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

Yeah, I do. Actually, that's kind of the main reason I came in. I just keep beating myself up lately. I've been convinced that I'm not really senior material at work, you know? Like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

I work as a computer systems analyst, and we just rolled out this massive server migration last month. I mean, it was a nightmare. We were supposed to transition everything over the weekend to minimize downtime, but the legacy database wouldn't sync properly with the new cloud infrastructure. I told my manager, Dave, that we needed to run a parallel test environment first. But Dave—he's this guy who always wears these really loud, patterned golf shirts to the office, even in January. Like, neon green and pink argyle. He insists he gets them custom made from this tailor in Florida. Anyway, Dave didn't want to wait because the VP of Operations was breathing down his neck. The VP is this intense woman who used to work in finance and always talks in sports metaphors. Everything is a "touchdown" or a "fumble." She brought in these stale donuts from a place down the street on the morning of the launch, like that was going to make up for the fact that we were all running on three hours of sleep...

But, uh... sorry, I lost my train of thought. Guilt, right. Yeah, I just feel like a fraud at work, like I've tricked them all and I'm just letting everyone down.
Do you ever have days where you feel completely normal and your low feelings are gone?

Well, I mean... no, not really. Not completely normal. Looking back, these low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now. It's just this heavy feeling that doesn't really lift. 

I remember it started right around the time my sister adopted her rescue dog. It's this mix, they think part terrier, part something else, maybe beagle? He has these huge floppy ears that don't quite match his head. She named him Barnaby. Anyway, she got him from this shelter two towns over, and the facility was right next to an old drive-in movie theater that got shut down in the late nineties. I used to go there when I was a teenager. We'd sneak people in by hiding them in the trunk of my buddy Mike's Chevy Cavalier. Which was incredibly dangerous, now that I think about it. Mike was a terrible driver. He actually backed into a fire hydrant once outside the Dairy Queen and tried to convince the cops the hydrant was placed illegally. He had this whole theory about municipal zoning laws that he read about on some internet forum...

But, um... yeah. Normal days. Not really. It's been about eleven months of just feeling down and guilty like this.
Are your low feelings present every day, or do they come and go?

Yeah, it's pretty much most days lately. I've had this heavy, low feeling, like I'm just moving through work and home with the color turned down, you know? 

It's kind of like watching an old TV where the tint is off. My grandparents had one of those massive wooden console TVs in their living room when I was growing up. The thing must have weighed three hundred pounds. My grandfather refused to get rid of it even when the picture started turning completely green. He'd sit in his La-Z-Boy—this awful plaid monstrosity that smelled like pipe tobacco and old newspapers—and watch Jeopardy every single night at 7:00 PM on the dot. He was obsessed with Alex Trebek. He actually wrote a letter to the network once complaining about a clue they gave about the Battle of Gettysburg, because he was a huge Civil War buff. He used to build these incredibly detailed dioramas in the basement with tiny hand-painted lead soldiers. He'd spend hours getting the terrain just right using papier-mâché and real dirt from the backyard, which drove my grandmother crazy because he kept tracking mud onto her white carpets...

But, uh... yeah. Most days. It's just a constant, heavy feeling. Like the color is just gone.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or wished you were dead?

I haven't made any plans or anything like that, but... yeah, sometimes I do catch myself thinking it might just be easier if I didn't wake up some morning. Just to not have to deal with it all. 

It reminds me of this one time my alarm clock broke when I was in high school. It was this old digital thing with those red LED numbers, you know? And the power went out during a thunderstorm. The storm was crazy, lightning hit this massive oak tree at the end of our street and split it right down the middle. The city had to come with chainsaws the next day, and it blocked traffic for hours. Our neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she was furious because she couldn't get her Cadillac out of the driveway to go to her weekly bridge game. She played with these three other ladies who all wore matching tracksuits. Anyway, the alarm didn't go off, and I just slept through the whole morning. It was so peaceful, just not having to wake up and face the day, not having to go to Mr. Henderson's history class. Mr. Henderson had this habit of pacing back and forth while he talked, and he'd always jingle the loose change in his pocket. It drove me absolutely insane. He'd just pace and jingle, pace and jingle...

But, um... yeah. I don't want to hurt myself. I just... sometimes I wish I could just sleep and not wake up.
Have you ever thought about how you would hurt yourself if you were to act on those thoughts of not waking up?

No, no, I haven't... I haven't made any plans or thought about how I would do it or anything like that. It's not like a scheme I'm hatching. It's really just that passing thought, you know? Like, it might just be easier if I just didn't wake up some morning. 

Speaking of waking up, my mattress is getting so old, I think there's a spring poking through right where my lower back hits. I bought it at this liquidation sale about eight years ago when that big department store downtown went out of business. The whole building is still empty, actually. They keep talking about turning it into luxury condos, but the zoning board keeps fighting with the developers over parking requirements. My buddy Dave works for the city planning office, and he says the developer is this guy who made his fortune selling imported tile, and he's incredibly stubborn. Dave said the guy showed up to a city council meeting in a full tuxedo once, just to make a point about... I don't even know what. Dave has the craziest stories. He used to be a bartender before he got into city planning, worked at this dive bar called The Rusty Anchor that had peanut shells all over the floor. You'd just throw them right on the ground...

But anyway, to answer your question... no plans. Just that feeling that not waking up would be easier.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Well, I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, maybe doing a little fishing, or just putting on a record. But lately, I just... I leave all the stuff sitting there. I don't really care. 

I've got this beautiful vintage Weber grill, the classic kettle kind. I found it at a garage sale a few years back for, like, twenty bucks. The guy selling it was moving to Arizona because his daughter just had twins out there and he wanted to be closer to them. He had all this incredible stuff he was just practically giving away. He even had a complete set of original Star Wars action figures still in the packaging, but some collector bought them right before I got there. The collector drove this bright yellow Volkswagen Beetle, which you don't see much anymore. I remember my aunt had a Beetle when I was a kid, but hers was powder blue. She used to drive me to the public pool in it every summer. We'd listen to the Beach Boys on an 8-track player she installed herself. She was surprisingly handy with cars, actually. She rebuilt the carburetor on that thing twice...

But yeah, the grill just sits there now. The records too. I just don't have the energy for it.
Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past month?

I don't know the exact percentage, but my belt is definitely fitting a little looser these days. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, it's just... my appetite has been totally off. I'll just grab a few bites of something here and there, or completely skip supper. 

It's funny I mention the belt, actually. It's this really nice leather one I got at a craft fair up in the mountains a couple of years ago. The guy who made it had this huge beard and was wearing overalls, looked exactly like a lumberjack. He was selling all these hand-tooled leather goods out of the back of this old, converted school bus. He told me he and his wife bought the bus at an auction in Oregon and spent two years turning it into a mobile workshop and home. They had solar panels on the roof and a little wood stove inside. His wife made these incredible stained glass suncatchers. I bought one shaped like a hummingbird for my sister, but I ended up dropping it in the parking lot on the way to my car. It shattered everywhere. The parking lot was gravel, so it was a nightmare trying to pick up all those little pieces of colored glass. I spent like twenty minutes on my hands and knees just trying to make sure nobody's tires would get punctured. A guy in a pickup truck actually stopped to help me, he had this golden retriever in the passenger seat that just stared at us the whole time, wagging its tail...

But yeah, I haven't been eating much. Just not really hungry for supper most nights.
Would you say that these low feelings and lack of interest in activities are interfering with your daily life and relationships?

Well, yeah, I guess it is interfering. I mean, I'm still making it to work, doing my job as a systems analyst, but I've had to double-check myself a lot more lately. It's like my brain is just moving through molasses. And I've definitely pulled back from friends and family. I just don't really trust my mood or my judgment right now, so it's easier to just stay away. 

Speaking of work, we just migrated to this new database system last week, and it has been an absolute nightmare. The vendor promised it would be a seamless transition, but of course, it wasn't. The guy they sent to train us, his name was Gary, he had this really distracting habit of clicking his pen the entire time he was talking. Click, click, click. It was driving me crazy. He said he used to work in cybersecurity for a bank in Chicago before he took this consulting gig. Chicago is a great city. I went there for a conference a few years ago and had the best deep-dish pizza of my life at this little place off the Magnificent Mile. The waiter told me the restaurant had been owned by the same family since the 1940s. They had all these black-and-white photos on the wall of famous people who had eaten there over the years. I think I saw one of Frank Sinatra, but it was kind of blurry. Sinatra always had such great style, you know? The suits, the hats. You just don't see people dressing up like that to go out to dinner anymore. Nowadays, people will go to a nice restaurant in sweatpants. It's just a different world...

But anyway, yeah, I'm still getting to work, just double-checking things a lot, and keeping to myself mostly.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns lately?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty messed up. Now I either wake up way too early, just lying there thinking about client tickets and system errors, and I can't get back to sleep... or I actually sleep enough hours and still wake up feeling completely worn out. 

It's frustrating because I used to be such a heavy sleeper. I remember back when I was a teenager, my dad bought this old riding lawnmower from our neighbor, Mr. Henderson. Mr. Henderson was this retired Navy guy who kept his lawn looking like a golf course. He used to edge the sidewalks with this weird tool he made himself out of an old shovel handle and a circular saw blade. Anyway, that lawnmower was incredibly loud. It sounded like a small airplane taking off. My dad would be out there at seven in the morning on a Saturday, just roaring back and forth right under my bedroom window, and I would sleep right through it. My mom used to joke that a bomb could go off and I wouldn't even roll over. She always made these huge Saturday breakfasts, though—pancakes, bacon, the works. She had this cast-iron skillet that belonged to her grandmother. She claimed that the secret to perfect bacon was never washing the skillet with soap, just wiping it down with a paper towel. I tried that once with a pan I bought at a camping supply store, but it just got really sticky and smelled like old grease. I ended up throwing it out. I think you really need the antique cast iron for that trick to work...

But yeah, sleep is just... it's either waking up at 4 AM stressing about work, or sleeping eight hours and still feeling like I haven't slept at all.
Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, my brain feels a little slow, like I said, but I don't think I'm physically moving or talking any slower. 

Though, you know, my uncle Dave used to talk incredibly slow. He was from East Texas, had this real thick drawl that just stretched every word out. He could take five minutes just to tell you what he had for breakfast. He used to drive this enormous, powder-blue Cadillac. It was a 1976 Eldorado, I think. The thing was like a boat. He kept it immaculate, washed and waxed it every single Sunday afternoon, right after church. He’d always listen to old Willie Nelson tapes on the 8-track player while he did it. I remember one time, the 8-track player ate his favorite tape—it was the Stardust album. He was so mad, he spent hours with a pair of tweezers and a tiny little screwdriver trying to splice the tape back together. He actually got it working again, but there was this one spot in the middle of "Blue Skies" where it would always skip and sound kind of warped. It drove my aunt crazy, but Dave just said it gave the song character. They lived in this ranch-style house that had shag carpet in every room, even the bathrooms. It was this weird avocado green color... 

But no, to answer your question, I don't think I'm moving or speaking slower. Just the regular pace, I guess.
Have you ever experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there, or seen things that others couldn't see?

No, no, nothing like that. I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there. I mean, my mind gets a little loud with all the worrying sometimes, but it's just my own thoughts, you know? 

Speaking of seeing things, though, did I ever tell you about the time I went camping out near Joshua Tree? The stars out there are just unbelievable. Because there's no light pollution, you can see the Milky Way so clearly it almost looks painted on the sky. I went with this guy I used to work with, Todd. Todd was a real character. He insisted on bringing this massive, heavy-duty telescope that he bought at a pawn shop in Vegas. He was convinced we were going to see UFOs. We spent like three hours trying to calibrate the lenses, and he kept adjusting the tripod because the desert sand was so uneven. He had this whole theory that the government uses old mining shafts out there to hide experimental aircraft. He even brought a Geiger counter, just in case. It never clicked once, obviously. But we did end up seeing a meteor shower, which was incredible. We made chili on this tiny little portable stove, and Todd accidentally dropped a whole bottle of hot sauce into the pot. It was so spicy we could barely eat it, but we were so hungry we just suffered through it. I think I drank about a gallon of water that night. I had to keep getting out of the tent to pee, and it gets freezing in the desert at night, like, bone-chilling cold...

But yeah, no voices or hallucinations or anything like that. Just my own regular thoughts.
Do you feel like you're moving or talking slower than usual, or do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

Well, like I said before, I don't really think I'm moving or talking slower. And I wouldn't say I'm restless either, like I can't sit still. I mean, I sit at a desk all day looking at code and system logs, so I'm pretty used to just staying in one spot for hours. 

Though, honestly, sitting still used to be a huge problem for my buddy Greg. I've known Greg since high school. We actually met in woodshop class. We had this teacher, Mr. Albright, who was missing half of his left index finger. You'd think that would be a cautionary tale, right? But Mr. Albright was the most relaxed guy ever. He'd just drink black coffee out of this chipped mug that said "World's Okayest Dad" and let us build whatever we wanted. Greg decided he was going to build a grandfather clock. Not a birdhouse or a bookshelf, a full-on grandfather clock. He spent weeks just sanding the mahogany for the casing. He was always tapping his foot or drumming his fingers on the workbench, just pure nervous energy. He actually ended up joining the Coast Guard right after graduation. Said he needed a job where he was always moving. I went to his wedding a few years ago up in Seattle. It rained the entire weekend, which I guess is normal for Seattle, but they had planned this outdoor reception on a boat. We all had to huddle under this canvas tarp eating soggy crab cakes. The DJ's equipment got wet and shorted out, so we just ended up singing sea shanties. It was actually a really great time, despite the weather...

But no, I don't feel restless or slow. I'm just sitting here, same as always.

patient.answer:
Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I came in because, well, I just keep beating myself up lately. I've got this job as a systems analyst, and I just can't shake the feeling that I’m not really senior material. Like I’ve just somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

Which is funny because I've been messing with computers since high school. Never even needed a college degree for it, you know? I built my first rig when I was, like, fifteen. It was this old Pentium setup with a massive CRT monitor that weighed half a ton. My mom made me keep it down in the basement because she said it ruined the feng shui of the house. She got really into feng shui for a few years back then. Bought all these little indoor water fountains and made us keep the bathroom doors closed at all times so the positive energy wouldn't flush down the toilet. I'm pretty sure she just liked making my dad move the heavy furniture around every weekend, to be honest. He actually blew his back out moving a mahogany credenza in '98... 

But, um, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I just feel like I've tricked them all into giving me responsibilities I can't manage.

I helped him with some of the low-voltage stuff for the temperature sensors since I know my way around a circuit board, but I told him he was crazy messing with the main breaker himself. Electricity is no joke. My uncle actually got a nasty shock once trying to fix a toaster while it was still plugged in. Blew the transformer for the whole street. The power company was so mad... 

But, um... wait, sorry. Anxious. Right. No, I don't really get on edge about work. It's just more of a heavy, sinking feeling that I don't measure up, you know? Not really an on-edge kind of thing.

doctor.intent: determine presence of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you often feel sad or depressed?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days lately I’ve had this heavy, low feeling, like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks 'Do you often feel sad or depressed?', which corresponds to the symptom of depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess you could say that. Most days lately I’ve just had this heavy, low feeling... like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down, you know? 

Actually, speaking of the color being turned down, it kind of reminds me of this old TV my grandparents used to have. It was one of those massive wooden console ones from the seventies. The color tube started going out on it, so everything had this weird, faded gray tone. We watched the '86 World Series on that thing, and you couldn't even tell the Mets' uniforms had blue in them. My grandfather refused to buy a new one because he said they didn't make them like they used to. He was a mechanic—worked on diesel engines his whole life—so he thought he could fix anything. He spent three weekends trying to solder a new capacitor onto the board of that TV, and ended up just melting half the plastic casing. My grandmother was so mad. She wouldn't let him watch his bowling tournaments in the living room for a month... 

But, uh... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling sad. Yeah, just... just that heavy, faded feeling. Like I said.

inference.note: Added F32.9 as the patient reports a heavy, low feeling and feeling sad or depressed, which could indicate a depressive disorder. Ruled out F40.8 and F48.8 as the patient's symptoms do not clearly align with anxiety disorders or other neurotic disorders.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, fishing, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don’t really care.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient still enjoys things they used to like, which corresponds to the 'Loss_of_Interest' symptom.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I mean, usually I really look forward to grilling on the weekend, or maybe going fishing, or just putting on a record. But lately, I just leave all that stuff sitting there and I don't really care. 

Which is a shame, because I have this really nice offset smoker. I got it a few years back. My neighbor, Gary, he saw it and immediately had to go out and buy a way more expensive pellet grill. Gary's just one of those guys who has to one-up everyone, you know? Like last winter, I bought a snowblower, and two days later he’s got this massive two-stage beast that could clear an airport runway. Anyway, he tried smoking a brisket on that pellet thing for the Fourth of July block party last year, and he totally dried it out. Tasted like shoe leather. He blamed the butcher, but I saw him opening the lid every ten minutes to check it. You can't do that, you lose all the heat and the smoke. "If you're lookin', you ain't cookin'," that's what they say. My dad taught me that. He used to barbecue every single Sunday, rain or shine... 

But, um, wait. Sorry. Hobbies, right. Yeah, my grill is just sitting out there under the tarp right now. I just haven't had the interest to even uncover it or listen to any of my albums. Just don't care to.

inference.note: Added F32.0 as the patient reports a heavy, low feeling and loss of interest in activities, which are indicative of depressive symptoms. F41.9 was ruled out as the patient does not exhibit prominent anxiety symptoms.

doctor.intent: determine the duration of the patient's current depressive episode
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling this heavy, low feeling?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, the low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the patient has been experiencing the depressed mood ('heavy, low feeling'), which corresponds to the duration of the depressive episode.

patient.answer:
Looking back, I guess it’s been a while. Maybe around eleven months? I remember because it started right around the time we were doing this massive server migration at work. We were finally moving our databases off these ancient hardware blades to a cloud setup. My manager, Todd, insisted we do the entire cutover over a long weekend to minimize downtime. Which, you know, sounds great in theory, but it was a total disaster because the software vendor’s support team was on a skeleton crew. I told Todd we needed at least three of our own guys on standby, but he wanted to save the department budget on overtime. Typical Todd. He drives this leased BMW and always manages to slip his golf handicap into every conversation, but he doesn't know the first thing about actual network latency. 

Anyway, the migration script failed halfway through, and I spent 48 hours straight in the server room trying to roll back the system, just living on stale donuts and Diet Mountain Dew. I think I slept under my desk for two hours on a pile of ethernet cables. My neck was messed up for a week after that. I actually had to go to a chiropractor, which I usually think is a scam, but this guy had this weird table that sort of dropped out from under you...

But, uh... wait, sorry. I'm getting off track again. You asked how long. Right. Yeah, looking back to that migration, it was around then. So for about eleven months, off and on, these low, guilty periods have just been hanging around.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy most of the time?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, fishing, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don’t really care.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my loss of interest in normally enjoyable activities, which directly corresponds to the Loss_of_Interest symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I think we... didn't we just talk about this? But yeah, like I said, most of the time now I just don't care. I mean, usually I'd be all about firing up the smoker on a Saturday, or maybe heading out to the lake with my tackle box, or just throwing on some classic rock vinyl. But now? The grill's under a tarp, my rods are gathering dust in the garage, and I haven't touched my turntable in weeks. 

Speaking of the garage, I really need to get in there and reorganize. I have this whole pegboard system I started putting up, but I ran out of the right size hooks. I went to the hardware store—that big box one out on Route 9—and they were completely out of the two-inch straight hooks. The guy working in that aisle, he couldn't have been more than eighteen, he tried to tell me the curved ones would work just as well for hanging extension cords. I was like, kid, you clearly don't understand weight distribution. If you hang a heavy-duty outdoor cord on a curved hook, it creates a pinch point and damages the insulation over time. My old shop teacher, Mr. Henderson, drilled that into our heads back in high school. He was missing half his left index finger from a bandsaw accident, so when he gave you safety or tool advice, you listened. He used to drive this beat-up El Camino that he restored himself...

But, um... sorry. What was the question? Right, losing interest. Yeah, most of the time, I just don't have the drive to do the things I normally like. Just kind of leave it all sitting there.

doctor.intent: determine presence of significant weight loss
doctor.question: Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My appetite has been off, mostly grabbing a few bites or skipping supper, and my belt is a little looser even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about recent significant weight loss, which directly corresponds to the Weight_Appetite_Change symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, I'm not really trying to, but yeah, my belt is definitely a little looser lately. My appetite has just been off. Mostly I'm just grabbing a few bites here and there, or skipping supper entirely. 

Which is weird for me, because I usually love to cook. Like I was saying about the smoker. I actually have this great recipe for a dry rub that I use on pork shoulders. It's got smoked paprika, brown sugar, a little cayenne, and this secret ingredient—ground espresso beans. I got the idea from this barbecue joint my wife and I went to on our honeymoon down in Austin. Place was literally just a shack by the side of the highway, no air conditioning, just picnic tables out back. But the line was out the door by 10 AM. We waited for two hours in the blazing Texas heat. My wife got so sunburned on her shoulders, she had to wear my oversized t-shirt for the rest of the trip. We actually went to a pharmacy to get aloe, and the pharmacist there was this older lady who insisted we also buy this weird herbal tea she swore would help with the inflammation. Tasted like dirt and licorice, honestly. I don't know why we actually drank it...

But, uh... wait. Weight, right. Yeah, I'm not trying to diet or anything, but I've definitely lost some weight because I just haven't been eating much supper or having much of an appetite.

doctor.intent: determine presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that normally would bring you joy?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, fishing, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don’t really care.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about an inability to experience pleasure from normally enjoyable activities, which directly corresponds to a loss of interest or anhedonia.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean, I feel like we just covered this, but yeah. It's the same thing. I just... I don't get any joy out of it anymore. Like I said, normally I'd be all over grilling on the weekend, or heading out to fish, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don't really care. 

It's weird because I actually bought this new lure a couple months ago, right before I started feeling like this. It's this topwater frog lure, supposed to be incredible for bass when they're hiding out in the lily pads. I got it from this little bait shop near the lake. The guy who runs it, Sal, he's a character. Always wears these suspenders with measuring tapes printed on them. He was telling me about how the lake levels have been dropping the last few years because of some new dam project upstream. He said the Army Corps of Engineers completely botched the environmental impact study. According to Sal, they didn't even account for the migratory patterns of the local waterfowl, which is crazy because if you've ever been out there in October, the geese are everywhere. I mean, they make a huge mess on the docks. Last year I spent two hours power washing the community dock just so my wife wouldn't complain about slipping on... 

But, um... yeah. Pleasure. I just... I don't feel anything when I look at my grill or my fishing gear. It's just stuff now.

doctor.intent: determine presence of guilt or self-blame
doctor.question: Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep beating myself up that I’m not really senior material and that I fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I can.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of guilt, which directly corresponds to the symptom of worthlessness and guilt.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I do. Actually, that's kind of the main reason I came in. I just keep beating myself up lately. I've been convinced that I'm not really senior material at work, you know? Like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

I work as a computer systems analyst, and we just rolled out this massive server migration last month. I mean, it was a nightmare. We were supposed to transition everything over the weekend to minimize downtime, but the legacy database wouldn't sync properly with the new cloud infrastructure. I told my manager, Dave, that we needed to run a parallel test environment first. But Dave—he's this guy who always wears these really loud, patterned golf shirts to the office, even in January. Like, neon green and pink argyle. He insists he gets them custom made from this tailor in Florida. Anyway, Dave didn't want to wait because the VP of Operations was breathing down his neck. The VP is this intense woman who used to work in finance and always talks in sports metaphors. Everything is a "touchdown" or a "fumble." She brought in these stale donuts from a place down the street on the morning of the launch, like that was going to make up for the fact that we were all running on three hours of sleep...

But, uh... sorry, I lost my train of thought. Guilt, right. Yeah, I just feel like a fraud at work, like I've tricked them all and I'm just letting everyone down.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient's low feelings are consistently present or if they have periods of normal mood
doctor.question: Do you ever have days where you feel completely normal and your low feelings are gone?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, the low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there are periods where the low feelings are gone, which relates to the patient's experience of the depressive symptoms being 'off and on' over the past 11 months.

patient.answer:
Well, I mean... no, not really. Not completely normal. Looking back, these low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now. It's just this heavy feeling that doesn't really lift. 

I remember it started right around the time my sister adopted her rescue dog. It's this mix, they think part terrier, part something else, maybe beagle? He has these huge floppy ears that don't quite match his head. She named him Barnaby. Anyway, she got him from this shelter two towns over, and the facility was right next to an old drive-in movie theater that got shut down in the late nineties. I used to go there when I was a teenager. We'd sneak people in by hiding them in the trunk of my buddy Mike's Chevy Cavalier. Which was incredibly dangerous, now that I think about it. Mike was a terrible driver. He actually backed into a fire hydrant once outside the Dairy Queen and tried to convince the cops the hydrant was placed illegally. He had this whole theory about municipal zoning laws that he read about on some internet forum...

But, um... yeah. Normal days. Not really. It's been about eleven months of just feeling down and guilty like this.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's low feelings are persistent or intermittent
doctor.question: Are your low feelings present every day, or do they come and go?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days lately I’ve had this heavy, low feeling, like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency and persistence of my low feelings, which directly corresponds to the depressed mood symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, it's pretty much most days lately. I've had this heavy, low feeling, like I'm just moving through work and home with the color turned down, you know? 

It's kind of like watching an old TV where the tint is off. My grandparents had one of those massive wooden console TVs in their living room when I was growing up. The thing must have weighed three hundred pounds. My grandfather refused to get rid of it even when the picture started turning completely green. He'd sit in his La-Z-Boy—this awful plaid monstrosity that smelled like pipe tobacco and old newspapers—and watch Jeopardy every single night at 7:00 PM on the dot. He was obsessed with Alex Trebek. He actually wrote a letter to the network once complaining about a clue they gave about the Battle of Gettysburg, because he was a huge Civil War buff. He used to build these incredibly detailed dioramas in the basement with tiny hand-painted lead soldiers. He'd spend hours getting the terrain just right using papier-mâché and real dirt from the backyard, which drove my grandmother crazy because he kept tracking mud onto her white carpets...

But, uh... yeah. Most days. It's just a constant, heavy feeling. Like the color is just gone.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of suicidal thoughts
doctor.question: Have you ever thought about hurting yourself or wished you were dead?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up some morning.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thoughts of self-harm or wishing to be dead, which directly corresponds to the Death_Suicide symptom.

patient.answer:
I haven't made any plans or anything like that, but... yeah, sometimes I do catch myself thinking it might just be easier if I didn't wake up some morning. Just to not have to deal with it all. 

It reminds me of this one time my alarm clock broke when I was in high school. It was this old digital thing with those red LED numbers, you know? And the power went out during a thunderstorm. The storm was crazy, lightning hit this massive oak tree at the end of our street and split it right down the middle. The city had to come with chainsaws the next day, and it blocked traffic for hours. Our neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she was furious because she couldn't get her Cadillac out of the driveway to go to her weekly bridge game. She played with these three other ladies who all wore matching tracksuits. Anyway, the alarm didn't go off, and I just slept through the whole morning. It was so peaceful, just not having to wake up and face the day, not having to go to Mr. Henderson's history class. Mr. Henderson had this habit of pacing back and forth while he talked, and he'd always jingle the loose change in his pocket. It drove me absolutely insane. He'd just pace and jingle, pace and jingle...

But, um... yeah. I don't want to hurt myself. I just... sometimes I wish I could just sleep and not wake up.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of suicidal ideation with intent
doctor.question: Have you ever thought about how you would hurt yourself if you were to act on those thoughts of not waking up?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up some morning.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal plans or methods, which is directly related to the symptom of suicidal ideation or attempts.

patient.answer:
No, no, I haven't... I haven't made any plans or thought about how I would do it or anything like that. It's not like a scheme I'm hatching. It's really just that passing thought, you know? Like, it might just be easier if I just didn't wake up some morning. 

Speaking of waking up, my mattress is getting so old, I think there's a spring poking through right where my lower back hits. I bought it at this liquidation sale about eight years ago when that big department store downtown went out of business. The whole building is still empty, actually. They keep talking about turning it into luxury condos, but the zoning board keeps fighting with the developers over parking requirements. My buddy Dave works for the city planning office, and he says the developer is this guy who made his fortune selling imported tile, and he's incredibly stubborn. Dave said the guy showed up to a city council meeting in a full tuxedo once, just to make a point about... I don't even know what. Dave has the craziest stories. He used to be a bartender before he got into city planning, worked at this dive bar called The Rusty Anchor that had peanut shells all over the floor. You'd just throw them right on the ground...

But anyway, to answer your question... no plans. Just that feeling that not waking up would be easier.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, fishing, or putting on a record, but lately I just leave the stuff sitting there and don’t really care.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about my ability to enjoy or find pleasure in activities, which assesses for anhedonia or loss of interest.

patient.answer:
Well, I usually look forward to grilling on the weekend, maybe doing a little fishing, or just putting on a record. But lately, I just... I leave all the stuff sitting there. I don't really care. 

I've got this beautiful vintage Weber grill, the classic kettle kind. I found it at a garage sale a few years back for, like, twenty bucks. The guy selling it was moving to Arizona because his daughter just had twins out there and he wanted to be closer to them. He had all this incredible stuff he was just practically giving away. He even had a complete set of original Star Wars action figures still in the packaging, but some collector bought them right before I got there. The collector drove this bright yellow Volkswagen Beetle, which you don't see much anymore. I remember my aunt had a Beetle when I was a kid, but hers was powder blue. She used to drive me to the public pool in it every summer. We'd listen to the Beach Boys on an 8-track player she installed herself. She was surprisingly handy with cars, actually. She rebuilt the carburetor on that thing twice...

But yeah, the grill just sits there now. The records too. I just don't have the energy for it.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of significant weight loss
doctor.question: Have you lost more than 5% of your body weight over the past month?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My appetite has been off, mostly grabbing a few bites or skipping supper, and my belt is a little looser even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about weight loss, which is directly addressed by the Weight_Appetite_Change symptom.

patient.answer:
I don't know the exact percentage, but my belt is definitely fitting a little looser these days. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, it's just... my appetite has been totally off. I'll just grab a few bites of something here and there, or completely skip supper. 

It's funny I mention the belt, actually. It's this really nice leather one I got at a craft fair up in the mountains a couple of years ago. The guy who made it had this huge beard and was wearing overalls, looked exactly like a lumberjack. He was selling all these hand-tooled leather goods out of the back of this old, converted school bus. He told me he and his wife bought the bus at an auction in Oregon and spent two years turning it into a mobile workshop and home. They had solar panels on the roof and a little wood stove inside. His wife made these incredible stained glass suncatchers. I bought one shaped like a hummingbird for my sister, but I ended up dropping it in the parking lot on the way to my car. It shattered everywhere. The parking lot was gravel, so it was a nightmare trying to pick up all those little pieces of colored glass. I spent like twenty minutes on my hands and knees just trying to make sure nobody's tires would get punctured. A guy in a pickup truck actually stopped to help me, he had this golden retriever in the passenger seat that just stared at us the whole time, wagging its tail...

But yeah, I haven't been eating much. Just not really hungry for supper most nights.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms to differentiate between mild, moderate, and unspecified depressive episodes
doctor.question: Would you say that these low feelings and lack of interest in activities are interfering with your daily life and relationships?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still making it to work, but I’ve had to double-check myself more and I’ve pulled back from friends and family because I don’t trust my mood or my judgment lately.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how my symptoms are interfering with my daily life and relationships, which corresponds to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, I guess it is interfering. I mean, I'm still making it to work, doing my job as a systems analyst, but I've had to double-check myself a lot more lately. It's like my brain is just moving through molasses. And I've definitely pulled back from friends and family. I just don't really trust my mood or my judgment right now, so it's easier to just stay away. 

Speaking of work, we just migrated to this new database system last week, and it has been an absolute nightmare. The vendor promised it would be a seamless transition, but of course, it wasn't. The guy they sent to train us, his name was Gary, he had this really distracting habit of clicking his pen the entire time he was talking. Click, click, click. It was driving me crazy. He said he used to work in cybersecurity for a bank in Chicago before he took this consulting gig. Chicago is a great city. I went there for a conference a few years ago and had the best deep-dish pizza of my life at this little place off the Magnificent Mile. The waiter told me the restaurant had been owned by the same family since the 1940s. They had all these black-and-white photos on the wall of famous people who had eaten there over the years. I think I saw one of Frank Sinatra, but it was kind of blurry. Sinatra always had such great style, you know? The suits, the hats. You just don't see people dressing up like that to go out to dinner anymore. Nowadays, people will go to a nice restaurant in sweatpants. It's just a different world...

But anyway, yeah, I'm still getting to work, just double-checking things a lot, and keeping to myself mostly.

doctor.intent: determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns lately?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Now I either wake up way too early thinking about client tickets and can’t get back to sleep, or I sleep enough hours and still feel worn out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about significant changes in sleep patterns, which directly matches the Sleep Disturbance symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah, my sleep has been pretty messed up. Now I either wake up way too early, just lying there thinking about client tickets and system errors, and I can't get back to sleep... or I actually sleep enough hours and still wake up feeling completely worn out. 

It's frustrating because I used to be such a heavy sleeper. I remember back when I was a teenager, my dad bought this old riding lawnmower from our neighbor, Mr. Henderson. Mr. Henderson was this retired Navy guy who kept his lawn looking like a golf course. He used to edge the sidewalks with this weird tool he made himself out of an old shovel handle and a circular saw blade. Anyway, that lawnmower was incredibly loud. It sounded like a small airplane taking off. My dad would be out there at seven in the morning on a Saturday, just roaring back and forth right under my bedroom window, and I would sleep right through it. My mom used to joke that a bomb could go off and I wouldn't even roll over. She always made these huge Saturday breakfasts, though—pancakes, bacon, the works. She had this cast-iron skillet that belonged to her grandmother. She claimed that the secret to perfect bacon was never washing the skillet with soap, just wiping it down with a paper towel. I tried that once with a pan I bought at a camping supply store, but it just got really sticky and smelled like old grease. I ended up throwing it out. I think you really need the antique cast iron for that trick to work...

But yeah, sleep is just... it's either waking up at 4 AM stressing about work, or sleeping eight hours and still feeling like I haven't slept at all.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychomotor retardation
doctor.question: Do you find yourself moving or speaking more slowly than you used to?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor retardation (moving or speaking more slowly), which is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, my brain feels a little slow, like I said, but I don't think I'm physically moving or talking any slower. 

Though, you know, my uncle Dave used to talk incredibly slow. He was from East Texas, had this real thick drawl that just stretched every word out. He could take five minutes just to tell you what he had for breakfast. He used to drive this enormous, powder-blue Cadillac. It was a 1976 Eldorado, I think. The thing was like a boat. He kept it immaculate, washed and waxed it every single Sunday afternoon, right after church. He’d always listen to old Willie Nelson tapes on the 8-track player while he did it. I remember one time, the 8-track player ate his favorite tape—it was the Stardust album. He was so mad, he spent hours with a pair of tweezers and a tiny little screwdriver trying to splice the tape back together. He actually got it working again, but there was this one spot in the middle of "Blue Skies" where it would always skip and sound kind of warped. It drove my aunt crazy, but Dave just said it gave the song character. They lived in this ranch-style house that had shag carpet in every room, even the bathrooms. It was this weird avocado green color... 

But no, to answer your question, I don't think I'm moving or speaking slower. Just the regular pace, I guess.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there, or seen things that others couldn't see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or delusions), which are not included in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, no, nothing like that. I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there. I mean, my mind gets a little loud with all the worrying sometimes, but it's just my own thoughts, you know? 

Speaking of seeing things, though, did I ever tell you about the time I went camping out near Joshua Tree? The stars out there are just unbelievable. Because there's no light pollution, you can see the Milky Way so clearly it almost looks painted on the sky. I went with this guy I used to work with, Todd. Todd was a real character. He insisted on bringing this massive, heavy-duty telescope that he bought at a pawn shop in Vegas. He was convinced we were going to see UFOs. We spent like three hours trying to calibrate the lenses, and he kept adjusting the tripod because the desert sand was so uneven. He had this whole theory that the government uses old mining shafts out there to hide experimental aircraft. He even brought a Geiger counter, just in case. It never clicked once, obviously. But we did end up seeing a meteor shower, which was incredible. We made chili on this tiny little portable stove, and Todd accidentally dropped a whole bottle of hot sauce into the pot. It was so spicy we could barely eat it, but we were so hungry we just suffered through it. I think I drank about a gallon of water that night. I had to keep getting out of the tent to pee, and it gets freezing in the desert at night, like, bone-chilling cold...

But yeah, no voices or hallucinations or anything like that. Just my own regular thoughts.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychomotor agitation or retardation
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're moving or talking slower than usual, or do you feel restless and unable to sit still?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about psychomotor retardation (moving or talking slower) or psychomotor agitation (feeling restless and unable to sit still) during the depressive episode, which is not present in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Well, like I said before, I don't really think I'm moving or talking slower. And I wouldn't say I'm restless either, like I can't sit still. I mean, I sit at a desk all day looking at code and system logs, so I'm pretty used to just staying in one spot for hours. 

Though, honestly, sitting still used to be a huge problem for my buddy Greg. I've known Greg since high school. We actually met in woodshop class. We had this teacher, Mr. Albright, who was missing half of his left index finger. You'd think that would be a cautionary tale, right? But Mr. Albright was the most relaxed guy ever. He'd just drink black coffee out of this chipped mug that said "World's Okayest Dad" and let us build whatever we wanted. Greg decided he was going to build a grandfather clock. Not a birdhouse or a bookshelf, a full-on grandfather clock. He spent weeks just sanding the mahogany for the casing. He was always tapping his foot or drumming his fingers on the workbench, just pure nervous energy. He actually ended up joining the Coast Guard right after graduation. Said he needed a job where he was always moving. I went to his wedding a few years ago up in Seattle. It rained the entire weekend, which I guess is normal for Seattle, but they had planned this outdoor reception on a boat. We all had to huddle under this canvas tarp eating soggy crab cakes. The DJ's equipment got wet and shorted out, so we just ended up singing sea shanties. It was actually a really great time, despite the weather...

But no, I don't feel restless or slow. I'm just sitting here, same as always.
